overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: referring to the properties as "1,000 Acres" in the Purpose 6 notice was sufficient, though a close question. Two new allegations raised only on further review were declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session notice for a Purpose 6 real estate discussion failed to identify the properties, which were listed collectively as "1,000 Acres".
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find, based on the totality of the information before us, including the fact that the Complainant does not allege that any individual, including herself, was in fact confused by the notice topic, that the term “1,000 Acres” sufficiently identified the properties the Board anticipated discussing during its November 29 executive session.

allegations.summary: Request for further review alleged the Board did not establish a proper Purpose 6 basis for its November 29 executive session in its response to the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Because neither allegation was raised in an original complaint filed with the Board, we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Request for further review alleged the Board did not meet to review the complaint and delegate authority to respond before counsel responded.
allegations.key_passage: we remind the Board that although it may delegate authority to respond to a complaint, it must first meet to review the complaint and authorize such delegation.
